summary.text: 国, “country,” is a simplified form of 國. The outer enclosure remains, while the inner 或 has been replaced by 玉. Remembering the modern shape as “jade within borders” may help, but the older character has a different explanation: an enclosure supplies meaning and 或 supplies sound.

history.text: For 國, the phonetic analysis in Dong Chinese and Wiktionary connects 囗, an enclosure, with 或 as a pronunciation cue. The Shuowen also records the pairing of 囗 and 或. These are accounts of 國; the 玉 inside 国 belongs to the simplified form and should not be projected back into that older structure.
